Definition: properly, the crop gathered, i.e. (by implication) the autumn (and winter) season; figuratively, ripeness of age
BiblicalUsage: Choreph is the winter, the season when the crop is gathered and the cold sets in, and it is also the ripeness of a life. The prophet speaks of winter houses and summer houses, God promises that summer and winter shall not cease, the king sits in his winter house with the fire before him, and Job remembers the days of his ripeness when the secret of God was on his tabernacle.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe winter in these verses is both a season and a stage of life, and God is Lord of both. I hold that the ripeness Job remembers is the autumn of a life lived with God, and it is worth more than the summer.
